discovery: Discovery of Bose-Einstein condensation of excitons (spontaneous interlayer phase coherence) in quantum Hall bilayers

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: many-body physics in low-dimensional semiconductor systems
motivation: In closely spaced GaAs double quantum wells at total filling factor one, electrons in one layer bind to holes in the other and form an exciton condensate with spontaneous interlayer phase coherence. MacDonald and Girvin, with collaborators, predicted this broken-symmetry state and its signatures. Eisenstein's experiments established it decisively: a giant Josephson-like peak in interlayer tunnelling, quantised Hall drag, vanishing counterflow resistance and Coulomb drag, and the demonstration of dissipationless exciton transport. This is the clearest realisation of a Bose condensate of electron-hole pairs in a solid, long sought since the 1960s. The work rested on remarkable heterostructure design, independent layer contacting and careful low-temperature measurement, which later inspired electron-hole bilayer and graphene-bilayer exciton condensation experiments worldwide. It shows how engineered low-dimensional materials reveal fundamentally new collective quantum states.
